s: This is Planet Money from NPR.
这是NPR的星球货币。
Announcer
It was a couple months ago.
这是几个月前。
Jane Black
John had the day off.
约翰有了假日。
John owns a line of 30 trucks that haul goods all over the US.
约翰拥有一系列30辆卡车，
Sarah Gonzalez
And on his day off, he got a call from someone on his team saying, um, we kind of lost a truck.
在休假日，他得到了他的团队中的某个人的电话说，我们失去了一辆卡车。
One of the drivers they had booked for a job, they don't know where on the road he is.
一个他们为工作预订的司机，他们不知道他在哪里。
Usually, you can track a trucker's progress, but this person's tracker stopped tracking.
通常，你可以跟踪卡车司机的进步，但这个人的跟踪器停止跟踪。
Black
In the middle of the night, so he looked like he was tracking.
半夜，他看起来好像正在追踪。
John
He was within range the day before.
他在前一天的射程内。
And then, all of a sudden, the driver just dropped off the map.
然后，突然间，司机刚离开地图。
Black
So we reach out to him and say, hey, what's the issue?
所以我们走向他，问，，有什么问题？
John
You're not tracking.
你没有跟踪。
They called over and over, but he never answered.
他们多次打电话，但他从来没有回答。
Gonzalez
They never talked to him again.
他们从来没有跟他说话了。
John
He never picked up the phone again.
他从来没有接到电话。
He was gone.
他已经走了。
Whatever was in that truck never arrived at its destination.
卡车里的任何东西都没有到达目的地。
Gonzalez
John quickly figured out it was stolen.
约翰很快发现它被盗了。
And the first thing he thinks is, what was in that truck?
他首先想到的是，那辆卡车里有什么？
Yeah, what is the product?
是的，该产品是什么？
John
What's the value?
这是什么价值？
What was the-- what was the load?
什么是-- 什么是负载？
Gonzalez
What did they steal?
他们偷了什么？
It was a turkey prod-- it was turkey.
这是一个子--这是子。
John
Oh.
，这是一个问题。
Gonzalez
Wait.
待一点。
It was a truck just full of turkeys?
这是一辆装满的卡车？
Yeah, 40,000 pounds of turkeys.
是的，40000磅的子。
John
Do you think that this person, like, stole a random load, and they opened it up, and they were like, oh, man, it's turkeys?
你认为这个人，像，偷了一个随机的货物，他们打开了它，他们说，，这是子吗？。
Gonzalez
I was really hoping for, like, computers.
我真的希望有电脑。
I think they know at this point.
我认为他们现在知道了。
John
How much is something like that worth?
这样的东西有多少钱？
Gonzalez
$102,000, is what that one was.
10万2千美元，就是那个。
John
That's a lot of turkey.
这太多了。
Black
And--
没有什么。
Yeah.
是的，是的。
Gonzalez
--John says cargo theft does get a little predictable around the holidays.
约翰说，在节日期间，货物盗窃确实有点可预测。
Black
Turkeys are hit around Thanksgiving.
在感恩节期间，火被击中。
Gonzalez
Yeah, turkeys will be hit.
是的，子会受到打击。
John
You'll get, you know--
你会得到，你知道的--
Stuffing?
填充？
Gonzalez
--during-- yeah.
John
Mashed potatoes?
的土豆？
Gonzalez
I was just going to go with--
我只是想跟--
John
Gravy?
格拉维？
Gonzalez
--pies.
狗狗。
John
Exactly.
确切的。
Mrs. Smith's apple pies.
史密斯太太的果饼。
Apparently, it's easy to know what products tend to come out of which cities and then hit those trucks specifically.
显然，很容易知道哪些产品往往来自哪些城市，
Gonzalez
I can tell you what ships out of East Peoria, Illinois.
我可以告诉你哪些船只从伊利诺伊州东皮奥里亚出发。
John
It's pork.
这是猪肉。
I can tell you if it's posted out of-- I forgot the name of the city in Iowa.
我可以告诉你，如果它是从-- 我忘记了爱荷华州的城市的名字。
It's beef jerky.
这是牛肉。
If it's coming out of this one town in North Carolina, like this particular load was, it's poultry.
如果它来自北卡罗来纳州的一个城市，像这个特定的货物一样，它是家禽。
Black
And this is not the only time that John's cargo has been targeted and hit.
这并不是唯一一次约翰的货物被攻击。
Gonzalez
Anything that moves in a truck on a US road is vulnerable to being stolen. $725 million worth of goods were reported stolen last year.
去年有725亿美元的货物被盗。
But not everyone reports theft, so industry groups estimate way more is stolen, like $10 to $20 billion worth.
但不是每个人都报告盗窃，因此，行业组织估计有更多的盗窃，价值10到20亿美元。
And food is a particularly attractive target because it's not like a computer, which has a serial number and can be tracked and is worth a lot of money.
食物是一个特别有吸引力的目标，因为它不像一个计算机，它有一个序列号，可以追踪，
Black
Food, once you eat it, it's just gone.
食物，一旦你吃了，它就消失了。
The evidence disappears.
证据消失了。
Food and beverage is the single fastest-growing category of cargo theft, up 47%, maybe because, as you might have noticed, food prices are rising.
食品和饮料是货物盗窃最快增长的单一类别，可能是因为，正如你可能注意到的，食品价格正在上升。
I have noticed, yes.
我注意到了，是的。
Gonzalez
And just a couple of weeks ago, $10,000 worth of beef was stolen.
几周前，被盗了价值1万美元的牛肉。
A big tequila truck's been hit.
一辆巨大的德基拉卡车被击中了。
Black
Half a million dollars worth of lobster and snow crab and oysters were hijacked.
一半百万美元的龙，雪和被劫持。
Gonzalez
In June, it was bourbon.
在6月份，它是酒。
Yeah, we talked to someone who lost a whole truckload of bourbon.
是的，我们和一个失去了一辆卡车的布尔本的人谈过。
Black
You know, we're talking a half of million dollars' worth of bourbon.
你知道的，我们正在谈论价值50万美元的白酒。
Rob Koch
Like, how many bottles are we talking?
比如，我们正在谈论多少瓶子？
Black
10,800 bottles, 1,800 cases, 18 pallets.
Koch
Ooh!
Black
Yeah.
是的，是的。
Koch
It was a full truckload of Noble Oak Bourbon.
这是一辆充满酒的卡车。
Also good for Thanksgiving.
也适合感恩节。
Black
We're going to get a whole Thanksgiving meal here by the end.
在结束之前，我们会在这里吃完整的感恩节。
Hello, and welcome to Planet Money.
您好，欢迎来到金星。
Gonzalez
I'm Sarah Gonzalez.
我叫萨拉·冈萨莱斯。
And I'm Jane Black.
我的名字是简黑。
Black
Jane writes about food and politics.
简写的关于食物和政治。
Gonzalez
And the backbone of our trucking industry, the system that enables trucks to move all our goods, your Thanksgiving meal, is under attack.
我们的卡车行业的骨干，让卡车运输我们的货物，你的感恩节饭，受到攻击。
Food, clothes, fertilizer, baby formula, turkeys-- you name it.
食物，衣服，肥料，婴儿配方，火，你愿意。
Black
Today on the show, the surprisingly complex ways thieves are taking off with our cargo and what they're doing with it.
今天的节目，惊人的复杂的方式，盗窃者带着我们的货物，
Gonzalez
Where some of this stuff is going, we were not expecting.
我们没想到这些东西会发生在哪里。
The people behind it organized and dangerous, which is why John, who lost that load of turkeys, asked us not to use his last name.
它背后的人是有组织和危险的，这就是为什么约翰，那些失去了子的子，他要求我们不要使用他的姓氏。
Black
I had a federal government employee call me, and they said, these are bad guys with guns and they will hurt you and your family.
我叫一位联邦政府员工打电话给我，他们说，这些有枪的坏人会伤害你和你的家人。
John
And I said, well, I know that.
我说，我知道。
[LAUGHS] I've been going through that for the last five years.
我已经经历了这五年了。
We've been trying to tell you they're bad guys.
我们一直试图告诉你他们是坏人。
When a whole truckload of one of your company's super valuable products suddenly vanishes, you tend to remember exactly where you were when you found out.
当一辆超级价值产品突然消失时，你倾向于记住你发现时的确切位置。
Black

Rob Koch, the bourbon guy, says it was 2:00 PM on Friday, June 5, the start of his favorite weekend of the year, when he and his girlfriend sail a boat with a team and race from Marina Del Rey in Los Angeles to Catalina Island and back.
罗布·科克，那个酒的家伙，周五晚上2点，6月5日，他最喜欢的周末开始，当他和他的女朋友搭乘一艘船，从洛杉矶的马里娜·德尔·雷 (Marina Del Rey) 到卡塔利娜岛，然后回来时。
Gonzalez
I just love it because in the middle, when you get to Catalina, everyone parties and has a really good time.
我只是喜欢它，因为在中间，当你到达卡塔利纳时，每个人都会聚会，很好玩。
Koch
And then the next morning, whether you're hungover or not, you're sailing back, and you're racing.
然后第二天早上，不管你有麻醉还是没有，你回来了，你在比赛中。
Rob was packing for the sailing race when he got an email from a colleague-- "See Below."
罗伯正在为帆船比赛打包，当他收到一个同事的电子邮件："看下面。"
Black
And what it said was a gut punch.
这里写的是一个肠道打击。
A lot of bourbon had just been stolen.
刚刚被盗了很多酒。
And I knew exactly how much it was worth.
我知道它的价值。
Koch
The company Rob works at, A21 Wine & Spirits, they're not like a Bacardi or a Diageo.
罗伯工作的公司，A21葡萄酒和酒精，它们不像巴卡迪或迪亚杰。
Gonzalez
They're smaller.
他们更小。
And a bunch of their Noble Oak Bourbon is now gone.
他们的一群贵族树布尔本已经消失了。
One of the worst things in this business is if you run out of product.
在这个业务中最糟糕的事情之一是，如果你没有产品。
Koch
And so I have to overproduce in order to catch up.
所以我必须过度制作才能赶上。
Rob is the COO of this company, OK?
罗伯是这家公司的首席运营官。
Gonzalez
So he is thinking about all of the ramifications.
所以他正在考虑所有后果。
We're not just talking I can flip a switch and suddenly produce another-- you know, another batch.
我们不只是说话，我可以翻开一个开关，突然产生另一个...你知道的，另一个批量。
Koch
I need more corks, caps, labels, bottles, all the dry goods.
我需要更多的，帽子，标签，瓶子，所有的干货。
And we have to pay for all of that before this--
在这之前，我们必须支付所有这些...
He holds up a bottle.
他拿着一个瓶子。
Gonzalez
--ends up on this shelf.
终于落在这个货架上。
Koch
I feel like you should just take a big swig of that now, just to, like, see how-- [LAUGHS]
我觉得你现在应该喝一口，只是为了看看..
Gonzalez
Yeah.
是的，是的。
Koch
[LAUGHS] Oh, god.
，上帝啊。
Yeah.
是的，是的。
Anyway, back to the day the bourbon disappeared, Rob is looking at this email, kind of spinning out.
无论如何，回到白酒消失的那一天，罗伯正在查看这封电子邮件，一种转变。
Black
And he's like, OK, I got to let the big boss know what happened.
他说，好吧，我必须让大老板知道发生了什么。
So I call Mark, our CEO.
所以我打电话给我们的首席执行官马克。
Koch
And he's like, OK, well, just a reminder, you know, this is alcohol, right?
他说，好吧，只是一个提醒，你知道，这是酒精，对吗？
You're going to have to report this to the proper authorities.
你必须向适当的当局报告。
Just get that going.
让它运行。
I said, OK, cool.
我说，好吧，好吧。
The proper authority was the FBI because the bourbon was crossing state lines.
合适的权威是联邦调查局，因为酒正在跨越州界限。
Gonzalez
So I research FBI.
所以我研究了FBI.
Koch
[LAUGHS]
现在，我们要做什么呢？
How do you call the FBI?
你叫FBI怎么说？
Gonzalez
[LAUGHS]
现在，我们要做什么呢？
Yeah.
是的，是的。
Koch
I've never done this before.
我从来没有这样做过。
What am I doing?
我在做什么？
OK.
没有问题。
So I call the FBI.
所以我打电话给FBI.
Was it Special Agent Wayne?
这是特工韦恩吗？
Gonzalez
[LAUGHS]
现在，我们要做什么呢？
Koch
Yeah, so my title is the special agent in charge for FBI Philadelphia.
是的，所以我的职称是联邦调查局费城负责的特工。
Wayne Jacobs
But you can call me Wayne, yes.
但你可以叫我韦恩，是的。
Special Agent Wayne Jacobs was the one who told us about the bourbon heist.
特别特工韦恩·雅各布斯是告诉我们关于酒抢劫的人。
Black
He oversees FBI cargo theft investigations in Philadelphia.
他监督联邦调查局在费城的货物盗窃调查。
And when we asked him, Where are all these stolen goods going? he said a lot of them get resold on Amazon, Etsy, places like that.
当我们问他，所有这些被盗的货物去哪里去了？他回答说，很多被在亚马逊，埃齐，等等上卖掉了。
But for food, like, you're not selling that on Etsy and Amazon.
但对于食物来说，你不会在Etsy和亚马逊上销售。
Gonzalez
Yeah, I think the important thing to remember is that not all the goods end up on these online marketplaces.
我认为重要的是要记住，并不是所有的商品都会在网上市场上。
Jacobs
They could be directed to other countries for consumption, right?
它们可以被转移到其他国家供消费。
Like on a ship?
比如在船上？
Gonzalez
Yes.
是的，是的。
Jacobs

A lot of our stolen goods, and even food, heads to a port, is put in a shipping container, loaded on a vessel, and is exported out of the country, sometimes with an accomplice at the port who helps smuggle the goods out.
很多被盗的货物，甚至食物，前往港口，在运输容器中放入，在船上装载，并出口到国外，有时与港口的同谋，帮助偷运出货物。
Gonzalez
This is, like, so convoluted!
这太复杂了！
Yeah, yeah.
是的，是的。
Jacobs
Now, not everything goes overseas.
现在，并不是一切都去海外。
Black
Wayne and other people in the food and trucking industries told us that John's stolen birds, or Rob's bourbon, or--
韦恩和其他食品和卡车行业的人告诉我们，约翰的偷走的鸟，或是罗伯的酒，或者--
Someone else's energy drinks.
别人的能量饮料。
Gonzalez
--those things could also end up unwittingly, or wittingly, at your local grocery store.
这些东西也可能会在当地杂货店无意中，或者无意中。
Black
Or they could be, like, served to you at a restaurant that doesn't ask questions.
或是，可以在一个不问问题的餐厅提供给你。
Gonzalez
Or they could be sold out of a truck in a parking lot somewhere.
或者他们可以从卡车里出售到停车场。
Black
That day, when Rob called the FBI to tell them about his stolen bourbon, no one had any idea yet where all that Noble Oak was headed.
那天，当罗伯打电话给联邦调查局，没有人知道那个高贵的树要去哪里。
Gonzalez
So he had to explain all of the details to whoever was stuck answering the phone at the FBI.
所以他必须向FBI中接电话的人解释所有细节。
And when he was done, Rob decided to go ahead and get out on the ocean to start his race.
当罗伯完成时，他决定走上大海，开始他的比赛。
He's halfway to Catalina Island when his phone rings.
当他的手机响起时，他就在卡塔利纳岛的半路上。
Black
It's the FBI calling him back.
联邦调查局打电话给他。
Yeah, and he was like, uh, one second, everyone.
是的，他像，，一秒钟，每个人都。
Gonzalez
I gotta take this, you know?
我必须接受这个，你知道吗？
Koch
[LAUGHS]
现在，我们要做什么呢？
I have, like, a kind of important call.
我有一种重要的电话。
Gonzalez
Yeah, it's a little important, guys.
是的，这有点重要，伙计们。
Koch
Maybe I'm going to have to do this, so--
也许我必须这样做，所以...
A part of this is a little cool and exciting for Rob.
这对罗伯来说有点酷而令人兴奋。
Black
He's telling the FBI what he thinks went down, and the FBI is like, no, no, we think we know what happened.
他告诉联邦调查局他认为发生了什么事，联邦调查局说，不，我们认为我们知道发生了什么事。
They said, typically, what we see is that this is more related to a cyber crime of some sort.
他们说，通常，我们看到的是，这与某种网络犯罪有关。
Koch
OK, cool.
好吧，很好。
I didn't know what that really meant in the beginning, but that's kind of where that went.
起初，我不知道这意味着什么，但这就是我们所做的。
Rob continues with his race, very stressed.
罗伯继续他的比赛，非常紧张。
Gonzalez
Does not sleep well that night.
那天晚上睡得不好。
Of course, that also could have been that, you know, we were partying, but-- [LAUGHS]
当然，这也可能是，你知道的，我们正在派对，但-- [笑]
Koch
I was drinking a lot--
我喝得太多。
Gonzalez
Eh, you know.
你知道的。
Koch
--of tequila that day.
在那天喝了德基拉。
Gonzalez
It's--
这是...
Koch
Maybe that had something to do with it.
也许这与此有关。
Gonzalez
It's part of the culture.
这是文化的一部分。
Koch
All right, enough about tequila.
好吧，就够了酒了。
Gonzalez
We're talking about bourbon.
我们正在谈论布尔本。
Rob said the FBI told him what likely happened to his bourbon was a new kind of cyber hacking, specifically targeting trucking.
罗伯说，FBI告诉他，可能发生了他的酒是新的网络黑客攻击，
Black
Today's cargo thieves aren't just sticking up trucks Bonnie and Clyde style, though that still happens.
今天的货物盗窃者不仅仅是起卡车的波尼和克莱德风格，
It's evolved.
它已经进化了。
It's not just people with bolt cutters.
这不仅仅是有螺栓切割机的人。
It's people with computers, hacking into the nerve center of the entire trucking industry.
那些有电脑的人，入侵了整个卡车行业的神经中心。
The nerve center is this thing called a load board.
神经中心是一个叫做负载板的东西。
Gonzalez
Now, these load boards are basically online bulletin boards that connect people who need stuff moved with the truckers who can move it for them.
这些装载板基本上是网上公告板，连接需要搬运物品的人和可以为他们搬运的卡车司机。
The way our food and goods move in this country all rests on these load boards.
我们的食物和货物在这个国家移动的方式都依赖于这些货架。
A company like Rob's will say, hey, I have a load I need picked up in Philly.
像罗布这样的公司会说，我需要在费城收拾一个货物。
I need it sent to New Jersey.
我需要把它送到新泽西州。
It weighs this much.
它重量这么多。
It needs to be a refrigerated truck or not-- whatever.
不管是冷藏卡车还是不...
And then people bid on the job.
然后人们投标工作。
Black
Certified truck drivers go on and say, yep, I want that job.
经过认证的卡车司机继续说，是的，我想要这份工作。
I will move that load for you.
我会为你移动那个货物。
These load boards are hyper competitive.
这些装载板非常有竞争力。
Gonzalez
The whole industry relies on speed.
整个行业都依赖于速度。
If someone's offering you work, you want to respond faster than the next trucker, right?
如果有人向你提供工作，你想比下一个卡车司机更快地做出反应，对吧？
So Rob's job went up on the load board, and they secured the trucker.
所以罗伯的工作上升到货物板上，他们确保了卡车司机。
Black
Now, here's where it got interesting.
现在，这是有趣的地方。
Koch
The bourbon load was picked up and was making its way to a warehouse in New Jersey, as intended.
布尔本的货物被收拾，按照预期前往新泽西的一个仓库。
Black
But then--
但然后...
The day the load was supposed to arrive, the broker calls the dispatcher.
当货物到达的那一天，经纪人打电话给调货员。
Koch
Eddie's the dispatcher.
埃迪是调度员。
Eddie, hey, where's our load?
埃迪，我们的货物在哪里？
It hasn't shown up yet.
它还没有出现。
The warehouse is telling us it hasn't shown up.
仓库告诉我们它没有出现。
When's it going to arrive?
什么时候会到达？
Eddie says, oh, it'll be there in an hour.
